titre: DC power supply is a specified appliance
acte: Order for Enforcement of the Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act (Cabinet Order No. 324 of 1962)
autorite: Cabinet of Japan; Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
article: Appended Table 1 (Re. Article 1, Article 1-2 and Article 2), item (ix), 4
citation: 4. DC power supply units (including those with an AC power source device dual use, limited to those with a rated capacity of not more than 1 kilovolt-ampere, and excluding those for testing wireless communication equipment and those with other special structures) 5 years
exigence: The seller must treat the charger as a specified electrical appliance when it is a DC power supply unit with a rated capacity of not more than 1 kilovolt-ampere, because that item is listed in Appended Table 1.
note: Article 1-2 of the same Order says specified electrical appliances are those listed in the left-hand columns of Appended Table 1. Item (ix) is limited to AC appliances rated 100 to 300 volts at 50 or 60 hertz; the charger label reads 100-240V 50-60Hz. The 5 years is the period of Article 9(1) of the Act for the certificate. The translation states its last version as Cabinet Order No. 96 of 2012: later amendments were not read.

titre: Conformity assessment by a registered body
acte: Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act (Act No. 234 of 1961)
autorite: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
citation: the Notifying Supplier shall, before their sale, have them assessed with respect to the following items (hereinafter referred to as a "Conformity Assessment") by an organization registered with the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry pursuant to the provisions of the following paragraph, and must obtain and retain the certificate set forth in said paragraph
exigence: Before sale, the notifying supplier must have the specified electrical appliance assessed by a body registered with METI and must obtain and keep the certificate.
note: Applies to specified electrical appliances only (see jp-denan-scope-dc-power-supply). The notifying supplier is the manufacturer or importer that notified its business under Article 3. The same paragraph has a proviso when a certificate for the same product type is already held and still within its period. The translation states its last version as Act No. 122 of 2011.

titre: No sale without the PSE labelling
acte: Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act (Act No. 234 of 1961)
autorite: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
citation: Any person engaged in manufacturing, importing, or selling Electrical Appliances and Materials must neither sell nor display for the purpose of sale said Electrical Appliances and Materials unless the labeling set forth in Article 10, paragraph (1) is affixed to said Electrical Appliances and Materials.
exigence: The seller must not sell or display the charger for sale in Japan unless the labelling of Article 10, paragraph (1) is affixed to it.
note: The Act does not use the word PSE; METI calls the Article 10 labelling the PSE labelling on its English page. Article 17(1)(i) of the Regulation for Enforcement (japaneselawtranslation.go.jp, law 3006) requires, for specified appliances, the mark of Appended Table 6, the name of the notifying supplier and the name of the conformity assessment body; the marks are drawings, so the diamond and circle shapes were not read as text and are not asserted here. The letters JET on the label were not checked against the list of registered bodies.

acte: Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act (Act No. 234 of 1961)
autorite: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
citation: All persons engaged in manufacturing or importing Electrical Appliances and Materials must, within 30 days from the commencement of such business, notify the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry of the following particulars in accordance with the Electrical Appliance and Material classification specified by Ordinance of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry
exigence: The person importing the charger into Japan must notify the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry within 30 days from the commencement of that business.
note: The obligations of Articles 8, 9 and 10 attach to this notifying supplier. The METI English page meti.go.jp/english/policy/economy/consumer/pse/index.html, read during this task, states that for imported goods it is the importers who are responsible, that no foreign juridical person may make the Notification of Import Business unless it has completed registration as a foreign company in Japan, and gives AC/DC Power Supply Units as an example of Specified Electrical Appliances (Category A); that page later answered HTTP 202 with an empty body to a plain client, so it is not used as the quoted source. How this applies to parcels shipped direct to consumers from abroad was not read.

titre: Radio equipment needs the technical conformity mark
acte: Radio Act (Act No. 131 of 1950), Chapter 3 technical standards, as explained by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
autorite: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC)
citation: To prevent interference in the use of radio waves, radio equipment used in Japan must conform to the technical standards listed in Chapter 3 of the Radio Act. (Whether a device conforms to the technical standards can be confirmed via the technical conformity mark (Figure 1).)
exigence: The seller must supply a laptop whose Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radio conforms to the technical standards of Chapter 3 of the Radio Act, which is shown by the technical conformity mark.
note: In the Radio Act (japaneselawtranslation.go.jp, law 3205) Article 4 requires a licence to establish a radio station, with an exception for low power stations that exclusively use radio equipment with a conformity mark, and Article 38-7(2) lets a dealer in products incorporating marked radio equipment affix the same mark to the product. The MIC leaflet at tele.soumu.go.jp/resource/j/others/wifi/en.pdf states that the 5.2 GHz and 5.3 GHz bands are for indoor use only. The numbers R 217-241406 and T D240049217 were not looked up in the MIC database.

titre: VCCI voluntary emission control for members
acte: VCCI Council Rules for Voluntary Control Measures (technical requirements VCCI-CISPR 32)
autorite: VCCI Council (private voluntary council, not a government body)
citation: Under the voluntary control measures by the VCCI Council, the member is obliged to conduct MME (multimedia equipment) testing to verify conformity with emission (interference) standards prior to shipment of a product on the Japan market.
exigence: A VCCI member must test its multimedia equipment against the emission standards before shipping it to the Japanese market; the scheme is described by the Council as voluntary control.
note: Source is the VCCI Council's own site, not a government site, because the scheme is private; no government text on VCCI was found. The obligation binds members only. The same page says the member must ship the product with the prescribed indication on the equipment and in the instruction manual. No statutory EMC obligation for the laptop in Japan was read.

titre: Conformity assessment before import or sale
autorite: Ministry of Science and ICT; National Radio Research Agency (RRA)
citation: Any person who intends to manufacture, sell, or import broadcasting and communications equipment, and machinery which causes electromagnetic interference or is affected by electromagnetic waves (hereinafter referred to as "broadcasting and communications equipment, etc.") shall, with regard to the relevant equipment, obtain certification of conformity under paragraph (2), registration of conformity under paragraphs (3) and (4)
exigence: Whoever manufactures, sells or imports the laptop must obtain certification of conformity or registration of conformity for it.
note: The quoted sentence continues with a third route, interim certification under paragraph (7). KLRI translation, stated on the site to be for reference only. The technical requirements listed in the paragraph include electromagnetic compatibility (Article 47-3). The RRA page rra.go.kr/en/cas/intro.do lists computing devices and peripherals under registration of compatibility. Which route applies to the MT7920 radio module, and whether the charger alone is in scope, were not read. The word KC does not appear in the quoted paragraph. titre: Indicate conformity assessment on equipment and packaging
autorite: Ministry of Science and ICT; National Radio Research Agency (RRA)
citation: he/she shall indicate the fact that he/she has undergone conformity assessment on the relevant equipment and the packaging thereof.

titre: Level 3 equipment registered and RCM marked
acte: Electrical Equipment Safety System (EESS), Level 3 in-scope electrical equipment; AS/NZS 4417.1
autorite: Electrical Regulatory Authorities Council (ERAC), EESS participating state regulators
citation: All Level 3 in-scope electrical equipment offered for sale must be registered by a Responsible Supplier with the EESS and be marked with the Regulatory Compliance Mark (RCM) in accordance with AS/NZS 4417.1. Only Responsible Suppliers who are registered can sell in-scope Level 3 equipment.
exigence: The charger, if it is Level 3 in-scope equipment, must be registered with the EESS by a registered Responsible Supplier and be marked with the RCM.
note: Scope read in the EESS document 'In-scope Equipment Definitions and Risk Levels v4.3' (eess.gov.au PDF): 'Power supply or charger' is ticked at risk level 3, defined as a household type device with an output not exceeding 50V AC or 120V ripple free DC for charging batteries or supplying separate equipment, excluding IT and audio visual equipment that uses the output to also transmit data not associated with a power supply or charger function. The same level 3 page requires a valid Certificate of Conformity from a recognised certifier. EESS applies in participating jurisdictions only. The code SAA-230413-EA on the label was not looked up.

titre: Responsible Supplier must be locally established
acte: Electrical Equipment Safety System (EESS), Responsible Supplier registration
autorite: Electrical Regulatory Authorities Council (ERAC), EESS participating state regulators
citation: The Australian or New Zealand based person or company must have a business presence in Australia or New Zealand to become a Registered Responsible Supplier.
exigence: The seller needs a person or company with a business presence in Australia or New Zealand to act as Registered Responsible Supplier, since an overseas company cannot register.
note: The sentence just before on the same page reads that an overseas based company cannot be registered on the EESS Registration Database. The page defines the importer as the first person or company in Australia or New Zealand in the supply chain, whoever handles customs. How this applies to direct shipments from China to consumers was not read.

titre: ACMA supplier steps and compliance label
acte: Radiocommunications Act 1992; Radiocommunications Equipment (General) Rules 2021; Radiocommunications Labelling (Electromagnetic Compatibility) Notice 2017
citation: Before you supply a product to the Australian market, make sure you: check the rules to follow show your product complies sign and keep records register as a responsible supplier label your product.
exigence: Before supplying the laptop to the Australian market, the supplier must check the applicable rules, show compliance, sign and keep records, register as a responsible supplier and label the product.
note: Same page: an importer brings a product into Australia for sale, and 'If you ship a product from an overseas distributor to a customer in Australia, we consider you an importer'; products with only overseas markings cannot automatically be supplied. ACMA's step 5 page says the compliance label is typically the RCM and must be no smaller than 3 millimetres in height. Scope for a laptop is by analogy with ACMA's own example of a TV with Bluetooth and Wi-Fi falling under the EMC Labelling Notice and the General Equipment Rules; the labelling notices themselves were not read. ACMA EMC rules for the charger alone were not checked.

titre: External power supply energy standard scope
acte: Greenhouse and Energy Minimum Standards (External Power Supplies) Determination 2014, under the Greenhouse and Energy Minimum Standards Act 2012
autorite: GEMS Regulator (Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water)
article: What products are covered? (refers to section 6 of the Determination)
citation: The Determination covers single output external power supply units with a maximum output power of 250 W or 250 volt-amperes (VA), that: are designed to supply power to other appliances have an AC input from mains supply have one extra low voltage output (either AC or DC) that is either at a fixed voltage or a user selectable voltage through a selector switch
exigence: The seller must determine whether the charger is a covered single output external power supply, in which case the minimum energy performance standards of the Determination apply to it.
note: Important scope limit read on the same page under 'What products are not covered?': devices capable of multiple output voltages that are not user-selected, such as 'quick charge' units that change the output voltage depending on the end-use product. The charger is a USB PD unit with 20.6V, 15V, 9V and 5V outputs, so it may fall outside the Determination; this was not decided here. For covered products the page requires a compliant performance mark and tests at 230 V AC; the level VI mark is on the label. The page states the product is under review. The Determination text on legislation.gov.au was not read.

titre: GST on low value imported goods
acte: A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999, low value imported goods rules, as explained by the ATO
citation: If you are a non-resident business and you sell goods into Australia with a customs value of A$1,000 or less, GST applies and you will have to collect this from your customer and send the GST to us.
exigence: A non-resident seller must collect GST from the customer and remit it to the ATO on goods sold into Australia with a customs value of A$1,000 or less.
note: Same page: the customs value is the sale price minus freight and insurance from the place of export; consignments over A$1,000 have GST, customs duty and clearance charges charged to the importer at the border; the seller may need to register for GST. Whether the laptop is under A$1,000 depends on its price, which is not known here. Any GST registration turnover threshold was not read on this page and is not asserted.

autorite: Radio Spectrum Management (RSM), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
article: Step 4: Complete a declaration of conformity for your product
citation: To certify that a product meets all compliance requirements, you need to complete a Supplier Declaration of Conformity (SDoC).
exigence: The supplier must complete a Supplier Declaration of Conformity for the laptop.
note: Same page: an SDoC is needed for all radio products under Level of Conformity 1 and all level 2, 3, A1, A2 and A3 products; it may be signed by a New Zealand based agent of an overseas manufacturer or supplier; products supplied under the Radiocommunications Regulations (Mutual Recognition: Australia) Notice 2008 do not need a New Zealand declaration. The level of conformity of the laptop was not determined. RSM step 6 says a supplier must register for a supplier number and that the rules are the same when websites are used to reach the NZ market.

acte: Radiocommunications Act 1989 product compliance framework, labelling requirements
autorite: Radio Spectrum Management (RSM), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
article: Step 7: Label your products, Using the R-NZ
citation: When the product is a radio transmitter in a class where the level of conformity is A1, A2 or A3, you need to use the R-NZ compliance mark, not the RCM.
exigence: The supplier must label the laptop with the R-NZ compliance mark if its radio transmitter is in a class with level of conformity A1, A2 or A3.
note: Same page: 'You must label any products you intend to sell with a compliance mark before you can supply them to the market'; for radiocommunications and EMC products at level of conformity 1, 2 or 3 the RCM is used; the R-NZ is a New Zealand only label for radio products not harmonised with Australia; the mark or the characters R-NZ must be no smaller than 3mm in height. Which level applies to the laptop was not determined.

autorite: Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI), Ministry of Economic Affairs
citation: No commodities subject to inspection shall be released from the production premises, nor be exported or imported, if they do not conform to inspection requirements.
exigence: The products, as commodities subject to inspection, must conform to the inspection requirements before they are imported into Taiwan.
note: Article 8 of the same Act: for commodities produced overseas, the obligatory inspection applicant is the importer. Scope read in the BSMI booklet 'Taiwan Commodity Inspection Schemes for Electrical and Electronic Products' version 1.87 (bsmi.gov.tw PDF f1768800988860), Appendix C-2: automatic data processing machines under code 8471.30.00.00.8, battery chargers for computer, communication and consumer electronics and other static converters (AC-DC adaptors) under 8504.40 codes, with Registration of Product Certification modules II and III. Which 8504.40 line fits the charger was not decided. The booklet says the authority only accepts applications from Local Suppliers.

acte: Taiwan Commodity Inspection Schemes for Electrical and Electronic Products, Information Booklet version 1.87 (under the Commodity Inspection Act and the Regulations Governing the Use of Commodity Inspection Mark)
autorite: Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI), Ministry of Economic Affairs
citation: All regulated commodities must bear the Commodity Inspection Mark before they can be supplied to the Taiwan market. Local Suppliers are responsible for ensuring that their regulated commodities are affixed with the Commodity Inspection Mark in accordance to the regulations stipulated by the Competent Authority
exigence: Each product must bear the BSMI Commodity Inspection Mark before it is supplied to the Taiwan market, and the local supplier is responsible for affixing it.
note: The laptop label shows BSMI R31018; no BSMI mark is in the list of marks seen on the charger, hence false. Article 12 of the Commodity Inspection Act also requires the obligatory inspection applicant to place the mark on the commodity's body. The booklet is BSMI guidance, last updated 19 January 2026 according to its cover.

titre: RoHS presence marking in BSMI identifier
acte: CNS 15663 Section 5 'Marking of presence', as applied in the Taiwan Commodity Inspection Schemes for Electrical and Electronic Products, Information Booklet version 1.87
autorite: Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI), Ministry of Economic Affairs
article: Chapter 11 Commodity Inspection Mark, Identification number of product certification for RPC Scheme
citation: As for those commodities subject to marking requirements stipulated in CNS 15663, Section 5 “Marking of presence” under the RPC Scheme, the identification number of which shall be included “the presence conditions of the restricted substance” (i.e., RoHS or RoHS(XX,XX)).
exigence: For commodities subject to CNS 15663 Section 5, the identification number of the Commodity Inspection Mark must include the presence condition of the restricted substances, shown as RoHS or RoHS(XX,XX).
marque: RoHS marking in the BSMI identification number
note: The laptop label shows 'R31018 RoHS'; nothing equivalent is in the list of marks seen on the charger, hence false. Same booklet: the restricted substances are Pb, Cd, Hg, Cr+6, PBB and PBDE, and Appendix C-2 lists CNS 15663 Section 5 for automatic data processing machines (8471.30.00.00.8) and for the 8504.40 charger and adaptor lines. CNS 15663 itself was not read.
